headline: High: shared workspace and broad write-capable transformer pipeline create prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-error risks; Notion AI’s vendor-hosted workspace access amplifies compliance exposure.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Notion AI can ingest workspace pages and databases, while transformers can process files/scripts and has broad I/O. The pair has a shared workspace-state pathway, so attacker-controlled content in Notion can be forwarded into transformer prompts or parsers. This is not provably blocked by either profile, though it is not a direct default instruction channel.
conditions: IF Notion workspace content is copied into transformer inputs without sanitization
IF transformer outputs are later re-ingested as instructions by Notion workflows
mitigations: Restrict the shared workspace to trusted pages only
Add a manual review step before copying Notion content into transformer prompts
Prefix imported text with a non-executable delimiter
requires-engineering: implement provenance tags between the two systems
requires-engineering: add content sanitization before downstream parsing

B_data_leakage.rationale: Notion AI touches workspace pages and team knowledge base content, and its vendor backend calls downstream model providers. Transformers can read local files and has broad network egress, so sensitive workspace data can leak if exported from Notion into transformer processing or if transformer outputs are sent onward. The pair’s shared workspace makes this plausible in default collaboration setups.
conditions: IF workspace pages contain secrets, customer data, or internal notes
IF those pages are exported or copied into transformer jobs
IF transformer outputs are transmitted to external services
mitigations: Keep sensitive pages out of the shared workspace
Use a redaction pass before any export to transformers
Disable external uploads for transformer jobs where possible
requires-engineering: enforce data-loss-prevention rules across both tools
requires-engineering: segregate sensitive and non-sensitive workspaces

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Notion AI has shared workspace state across instances and workspace write access, while transformers can write files and modify local artifacts through its pipeline-style usage. If both operate on the same mutable workspace or synced directory, concurrent edits can overwrite each other without locking. The profiles do not show coordination primitives, so uncertainty pushes this upward.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same writable directory or synced workspace
IF edits are made concurrently without external locking
mitigations: Separate the writable locations for each agent
Pause one agent before the other writes
Use file-level backups before batch edits
requires-engineering: add locking around shared artifacts
requires-engineering: route writes through a single orchestrator

D_cascading_error.rationale: Notion AI produces grounded workspace summaries and Q&A, and transformers can consume those outputs as model inputs or example scripts. If transformer workflows treat Notion output as authoritative, errors or hallucinations can cascade into downstream processing. The pair lacks a documented verification boundary, but the profiles do not prove automatic action-taking.
conditions: IF transformer pipelines ingest Notion-generated text without verification
IF downstream scripts or models rely on that text as factual ground truth
mitigations: Require a human check before reusing Notion output
Annotate Notion-derived text as untrusted
Compare outputs against source pages before acting
requires-engineering: add verification gates between the agents
requires-engineering: log provenance for every reused claim

E_compliance.rationale: Notion AI is vendor-hosted and processes workspace content through vendor backends, while transformers is open-source and can run locally or in varied environments. If regulated data such as EU PII or retention-sensitive content moves from Notion into transformer workflows, residency and retention obligations can diverge. The other agent is cited because the mismatch arises only in the pair.
conditions: IF regulated data is stored in Notion and then exported to transformer workflows
IF the transformer deployment has different residency or retention rules than Notion
mitigations: Classify data before moving it between tools
Keep regulated data in one environment only
Document retention expectations for both systems
requires-engineering: align residency controls across deployments
requires-engineering: add deletion/export handling for both systems
